_intent: ADR-0562's central layering rule: a `facade` crate reaches its own capability's `core` only through `ports`. This gate freezes today's violators and makes a NEW one impossible to ship (shrink-only). Keys are CARGO PACKAGE NAMES, not paths or buck2 target labels, so a future capability move does not invalidate the baseline and make the repair look like laundering.

scan._note: Capabilities are the top-level dirs that contain a `<cap>/facade/` tree. Detection statically parses `<cap>/facade/*/BUCK` for absolute labels of the form //<cap>/core/<pkg>:<target>. Verified 2026-07-26 to reproduce the authoritative buck2 uquery result exactly: 35 packages, identical per-capability split. A Cargo.toml scan does NOT reproduce it — intelligence/facade/worker carried the edge in BUCK with zero Cargo path-deps. That witness was the ONLY one and it was REPAIRED 2026-08-03 (the BUCK dep had zero source references and was deleted), so no BUCK-only edge remains today; the BUCK scan stays authoritative because BUCK is the binding build, NOT because a divergent witness currently exists.

facade_core_direct_dep.detail: facade crate depends directly on its own capability's core, bypassing ports (ADR-0562 central layering rule)

facade_core_no_ports_layer.detail: facade->core edge in a capability that has NO ports/ crates; ADR-0562 §10.6 declares this dependency-legal until a ports layer exists

_out_of_scope.cross_capability_facade_to_core: 12 packages / 21 edges reach ANOTHER capability's core (marketplace/facade/dev-cli alone reaches 9). That is a different rule with a different remedy and is deliberately NOT gated here; see the ADR.
